sentences.cn_text: 有句老话说，所有广告预算中有一半被浪费了——问题在于，没人知道是哪一半。
sentences.en_text: An old saying has it that half of all advertising budgets are wasted — the trouble is, no one knows which half.

sentences.cn_text: 在互联网时代，至少在理论上，这一比例可以大幅降低。
sentences.en_text: In the internet age, at least in theory, this fraction can be much reduced.

sentences.cn_text: 通过观察人们在网上搜索、点击和发表的内容，公司可以将「行为」广告投放给最有可能购买的人群。
sentences.en_text: By watching what people search for, click on and say online, companies can aim “behavioural” ads at those most likely to buy.

sentences.cn_text: 过去几周的一场争论凸显了此类精细信息对广告商的价值：广告商是否应该假定人们乐意被追踪并接收行为广告？
sentences.en_text: In the past couple of weeks a quarrel has illustrated the value to advertisers of such fine-grained information: Should advertisers assume that people are happy to be tracked and sent behavioural ads?

sentences.cn_text: 还是应该获得明确许可？
sentences.en_text: Or should they have explicit permission?

sentences.cn_text: 2010年12月，美国联邦贸易委员会（FTC）提议在互联网浏览器中增加「禁止追踪」（DNT）选项，以便用户可以告知广告商他们不希望被追踪。
sentences.en_text: In December 2010 America’s Federal Trade Commission (FTC) proposed adding a “do not track” (DNT) option to internet browsers, so that users could tell advertisers that they did not want to be followed.

sentences.cn_text: 微软的 Internet Explorer 和苹果的 Safari 都提供 DNT 功能；谷歌的 Chrome 预计今年推出该功能。
sentences.en_text: Microsoft’s Internet Explorer and Apple’s Safari both offer DNT; Google’s Chrome is due to do so this year.

sentences.cn_text: 2月，FTC 和数字广告联盟（DAA）达成一致，行业将着手响应 DNT 请求。
sentences.en_text: In February the FTC and Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) agreed that the industry would get cracking on responding to DNT requests.

sentences.cn_text: 5月31日，微软引发了这场争议。
sentences.en_text: On May 31st Microsoft set off the row.

sentences.cn_text: 它表示，计划随 Windows 8 推出的 Internet Explorer 10 版本将默认启用 DNT。
sentences.en_text: It said that Internet Explorer 10, the version due to appear with Windows 8, would have DNT as a default.

sentences.cn_text: 广告商对此感到震惊。
sentences.en_text: Advertisers are horrified.

sentences.cn_text: 鉴于人性如此，大多数人会沿用默认设置。
sentences.en_text: Human nature being what it is, most people stick with default settings.

sentences.cn_text: 现在很少有人开启 DNT，但如果追踪默认关闭，它就会保持关闭状态。
sentences.en_text: Few switch DNT on now, but if tracking is off it will stay off.

sentences.cn_text: 美国全国广告商协会首席执行官鲍勃·利奥迪斯表示，如果行业无法收集消费者偏好信息，消费者的境况会更糟。
sentences.en_text: Bob Liodice, the chief executive of the Association of National Advertisers, says consumers will be worse off if the industry cannot collect information about their preferences.

sentences.cn_text: 他说，人们不会收到更少的广告。「他们会收到意义更少、针对性更差的广告。」
sentences.en_text: People will not get fewer ads, he says. “They’ll get less meaningful, less targeted ads.”

sentences.cn_text: 广告商将如何应对尚不明朗。
sentences.en_text: It is not yet clear how advertisers will respond.

sentences.cn_text: 收到 DNT 信号并不意味着必须停止追踪，尽管一些公司承诺会这样做。
sentences.en_text: Getting a DNT signal does not oblige anyone to stop tracking, although some companies have promised to do so.

sentences.cn_text: 由于无法判断某人是真正反对行为广告，还是只是沿用了微软的默认设置，一些广告商可能会无视 DNT 信号继续追踪。
sentences.en_text: Unable to tell whether someone really objects to behavioural ads or whether they are sticking with Microsoft’s default, some may ignore a DNT signal and press on anyway.

sentences.cn_text: 微软为何单独行动同样不明朗。
sentences.en_text: Also unclear is why Microsoft has gone it alone.

sentences.cn_text: 毕竟，它也有广告业务，并表示将遵守 DNT 请求，尽管还在研究具体如何实现。
sentences.en_text: After all, it has an ad business too, which it says will comply with DNT requests, though it is still working out how.

sentences.cn_text: 如果它试图对几乎完全依赖广告的谷歌造成困扰，那么它选择了一种间接的方式：默认启用 DNT 能否成为行业规范尚无保证。
sentences.en_text: If it is trying to upset Google, which relies almost wholly on advertising, it has chosen an indirect method: there is no guarantee that DNT by default will become the norm.

sentences.cn_text: DNT 似乎并非 Windows 8 的一个明显重要卖点——尽管该公司此前曾在这方面将其某些产品与谷歌产品进行有利比较。
sentences.en_text: DNT does not seem an obviously huge selling point for Windows 8 — though the firm has compared some of its other products favourably with Google’s on that count before.

sentences.cn_text: 微软首席隐私官布伦登·林奇在博客中写道：「我们认为消费者应该拥有更多控制权。」
sentences.en_text: Brendon Lynch, Microsoft’s chief privacy officer, blogged: “We believe consumers should have more control.”

sentences.cn_text: 真会如此简单吗？
sentences.en_text: Could it really be that simple?
